area51-groom-lake-map.summary: A CIA map from the 1992 U-2 and OXCART history that marks Area 51 and Groom Lake beside the Atomic Energy Commission's Nevada Test Site. It was released in 2013 with the less-redacted history, a release widely reported as the US government's first acknowledgement of the base.

area51-skylab-memo.title: Skylab Photographs Area 51
area51-skylab-memo.summary: A 1974 memo to CIA Director William Colby reporting that Skylab astronauts had photographed the one place they had been told not to (the name is blacked out; it was Area 51), and that NASA wanted the picture released while Defense Department agencies wanted it withheld. Colby's handwritten note questions the need to protect it, since the Soviets had it from their own satellites, and asks what it really reveals.

area51-u2-nasa-cover.title: U-2 in Fake NASA Markings
area51-u2-nasa-cover.summary: After Francis Gary Powers' CIA U-2 was shot down over the Soviet Union on 1 May 1960, NASA said the plane had been doing weather research. To back the cover story, a U-2 was painted in NASA markings with a made-up serial number and shown to reporters at NASA's Flight Research Center at Edwards on 6 May 1960.

area51-have-doughnut.title: Project HAVE DOUGHNUT
area51-have-doughnut.summary: The 1969 tactical report on HAVE DOUGHNUT, the 1968 project in which Air Force and Navy pilots secretly flew a Soviet-built MiG-21 at Area 51 against US fighters to learn how to beat it. Israel had lent the jet, which it got when an Iraqi pilot defected with it in 1966.

area51-a12-oxcart.title: A-12 OXCART in Flight
area51-a12-oxcart.summary: An undated 1960s U.S. Air Force photo of the A-12 OXCART, the Mach 3 spy plane Lockheed built for the CIA and test-flew at Area 51 from April 1962. This aircraft, 60-6932, was lost at sea with CIA pilot Jack Weeks in June 1968, shortly before the program ended.

area51-d21-drone.title: M-21 Carrying a D-21 Drone
area51-d21-drone.summary: An undated U.S. Air Force photo from the 1964-66 test program of M-21 60-6940, a two-seat A-12 rebuilt as a mothership, carrying a D-21 reconnaissance drone on its back. On 30 July 1966 a D-21 struck the other M-21 as it launched, destroying both and killing launch officer Ray Torick; the drone was later launched from B-52s over China instead.

area51-sr71-film.title: The SR-71
area51-sr71-film.summary: A short U.S. Air Force film of the SR-71 Blackbird, the Air Force's two-seat reconnaissance version of the CIA's A-12, with air-to-air shots, cockpit instruments at about Mach 3 above 80,000 feet, a takeoff and a landing. President Johnson revealed the SR-71 in July 1964; the CIA history says he was meant to say 'RS-71'.
area51-sr71-film.credit: U.S. Air Force (Media Production Flight, 367th Training Support Squadron, Hill AFB)

The ideas included a fake Communist Cuban terror campaign in Florida and Washington, a faked attack on a civilian airliner and blowing up a US ship in Cuban waters; Kennedy rejected the proposals.

gadgets-insectothopter.summary: CIA Museum photo of the Insectothopter, a dragonfly-shaped micro drone developed by the CIA's Office of Research and Development in the 1970s to carry a tiny listening device. gadgets-camp-century-film.title: City Under the Ice (Camp Century)

jfk-schlesinger-cia-memo.title: Schlesinger CIA Reorganization Memo
jfk-schlesinger-cia-memo.summary: Kennedy aide Arthur Schlesinger Jr.'s memo after the Bay of Pigs proposing to split the CIA into an operations agency and a research agency, with clandestine work cleared by the State Department. jfk-mystery-man.title: Mexico City Mystery Man
jfk-mystery-man.summary: A CIA photo of an unidentified man taken in Mexico City in October 1963, which CIA staff at first wrongly linked to Oswald; it became Warren Commission Exhibit 237. The FBI showed it to Oswald's mother on 23 November 1963, and neither the CIA, the FBI nor the House Assassinations Committee could identify the man, who was neither Oswald nor Ruby.

jfk-air-force-one-tape.title: Air Force One Radio Tape

nuclear-operation-ivy-film.title: Operation Ivy
nuclear-operation-ivy-film.summary: Silent 10-minute National Archives reel of Operation Ivy, the Air Force film of Mike, the first full-scale hydrogen bomb test, with actor Reed Hadley as host. Mike yielded 10.4 megatons on 1 November 1952 and left a crater where the island of Elugelab had been; a censored version of the film was released to the public in 1954.

nuclear-sac-target-study.title: SAC Atomic Weapons Requirements Study
nuclear-sac-target-study.summary: Title page, contents and introduction of Strategic Air Command's June 1956 study of the atomic weapons it would need for a war in 1959. The full study listed more than 1,100 Soviet bloc airfields and more than 1,200 cities as targets, with 'population' as a target in cities such as Moscow, Leningrad, East Berlin, Warsaw and Beijing.

nuclear-castle-bravo.title: Castle Bravo
nuclear-castle-bravo.summary: Aerial photograph of the Castle Bravo fireball over Bikini Atoll on 1 March 1954, the largest nuclear test the United States ever conducted. Bravo yielded 15 megatons, nearly three times what its planners expected, and its fallout sickened Marshall Islanders and contaminated 23 Japanese fishermen.
nuclear-castle-bravo.credit: Defense Atomic Support Agency, National Archives (RG 374)

nuclear-starfish-prime.title: Starfish Prime
nuclear-starfish-prime.summary: Photograph of the Starfish Prime burst and the aurora it made, taken from atop Haleakala on Maui. The 1.4-megaton warhead exploded about 400 km above the Pacific near Johnston Atoll on 9 July 1962, and its electromagnetic pulse knocked out about 300 streetlights in Hawaii.
nuclear-starfish-prime.credit: Defense Atomic Support Agency, National Archives (RG 374)

presidents-smoking-gun-tape.title: The Smoking Gun Tape
presidents-smoking-gun-tape.summary: An eight-minute excerpt of the 23 June 1972 Oval Office meeting in which Nixon and his chief of staff, H. R. Haldeman, agree to have the CIA ask the FBI to halt its Watergate investigation on national security grounds. Its release on 5 August 1974, after the Supreme Court ordered the tapes handed over, ended Nixon's remaining support in Congress, and he resigned days later.
presidents-smoking-gun-tape.credit: White House taping system; Richard Nixon Presidential Library

presidents-pdb-bin-ladin.title: Bin Ladin Determined To Strike in US
presidents-pdb-bin-ladin.summary: The item in President George W. Bush's Daily Brief of 6 August 2001, five weeks before the 9/11 attacks, warning that Bin Ladin had wanted to strike inside the US since 1997 and citing FBI information on activity consistent with preparations for hijackings. It was declassified in April 2004 for the 9/11 Commission; this scan is from the CIA's September 2026 release of 71 declassified 9/11-related briefs.

presidents-situation-room.title: The Situation Room

satellites-corona-first-image.title: First CORONA Image: Mys Shmidta
satellites-corona-first-image.summary: The first photograph from a US reconnaissance satellite, showing a Soviet military airfield at Mys Shmidta on the Chukchi Sea, taken on 18 August 1960 by CORONA mission 9009, publicly called Discoverer XIV. CORONA imagery was declassified by executive order in February 1995.

satellites-hexagon-seabed-film.title: HEXAGON Film on the Ocean Floor
satellites-hexagon-seabed-film.summary: A Navy Trieste II photo of the film spools and gold-foil canister from a HEXAGON spy satellite capsule on the Pacific floor about 16,400 feet down, where it sank in July 1971 after its parachute failed. In April 1972 Trieste II hooked the film, but it broke apart on the way up and only about 25 feet was saved.
satellites-hexagon-seabed-film.credit: U.S. Navy (Trieste II), via Central Intelligence Agency

satellites-iran-launch-pad.title: Trump's Tweeted Spy Satellite Photo
satellites-iran-launch-pad.summary: A US reconnaissance image of the wrecked launch pad at Iran's Imam Khomeini Space Center after a Safir rocket exploded on 29 August 2019, which President Trump posted on Twitter the next day, saying he had 'the absolute right' to release it. Amateur satellite trackers matched it to USA 224, believed to be a KH-11 reconnaissance satellite.
satellites-iran-launch-pad.credit: U.S. government; posted by President Donald J. Trump

satellites-c119-air-catch.title: C-119 Air Catch of a CORONA Capsule
satellites-c119-air-catch.summary: An Air Force C-119 of the 6593rd Test Squadron from Hickam AFB, Hawaii, catching a parachuting CORONA film capsule in mid-air over the Pacific, the way spy satellite film came home. The squadron flew C-119s on these catches until 1962, and on 19 August 1960 one made the first mid-air recovery of a capsule returning from orbit, from Discoverer XIV.
satellites-c119-air-catch.credit: U.S. Air Force, via National Reconnaissance Office

satellites-corona-venezuela.title: CORONA Capsule Found in Venezuela
satellites-corona-venezuela.summary: Four Venezuelan villagers with the battered film capsule of CORONA mission 1005, which came down off course in 1964 on a farm near the Colombian border instead of being caught over the Pacific. Locals hacked at it for its gold parts before the US got it back that August, and afterwards CORONA capsules dropped their SECRET markings and carried a reward notice in eight languages.

satellites-point-in-time-film.title: A Point in Time: The CORONA Story
satellites-point-in-time-film.summary: A once-secret CIA documentary on CORONA, the first US photo-reconnaissance satellite program, covering why it was built and how the satellite and its cameras worked. Made by the CIA's film branch between 1972 and 1975 and opening with Director Richard Helms at the program's October 1972 museum dedication, it was first shown publicly in May 1995.

satellites-hexagon-recovery-memo.title: Deep Sea Recovery of HEXAGON RV 1201-3
satellites-hexagon-recovery-memo.summary: A 24 May 1972 CIA memorandum, with trip reports and photographs, on the effort to raise a film capsule from the first HEXAGON mission from 16,000 feet of Pacific water with the Navy bathyscaphe Trieste II. It records three dives, the film stacks being hooked on 25 April 1972, and the film breaking apart on the way up, leaving 25 feet.

space-moon-disaster.title: In Event of Moon Disaster
space-moon-disaster.summary: A memo from speechwriter William Safire to chief of staff H. R. Haldeman with the speech President Nixon would have read if Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin Aldrin were stranded on the Moon. It also told Nixon to telephone the "widows-to-be" and had a clergyman commend their souls to "the deepest of the deep".

space-jfk-webb-tape.title: "I'm Not That Interested in Space"
space-jfk-webb-tape.summary: Part 1 of the recorded Cabinet Room meeting in which President Kennedy pressed NASA Administrator James Webb to make the Moon landing NASA's top priority. In it Kennedy says he is "not that interested in space" and that the only justification for the cost is to beat the Soviet Union.
space-jfk-webb-tape.credit: White House recording, John F. Kennedy Presidential Library (via NASA History Office)

space-lunik-kidnapping.title: The Kidnaping of the Lunik
space-lunik-kidnapping.summary: A 1967 Studies in Intelligence article on how US intelligence officers examined a Soviet Lunik upper stage from a touring Soviet exhibition and found it was a real production vehicle, not a mock-up. On a second access they borrowed it overnight, copied its factory markings and returned it before the Soviets missed it.
space-lunik-kidnapping.credit: Sydney Wesley Finer, Central Intelligence Agency

space-n1-moon-rocket.title: Soviet N1 Moon Rocket from Orbit
space-n1-moon-rocket.summary: A KH-8 GAMBIT spy satellite photo of a launch complex at Tyuratam (Baikonur), Kazakhstan, showing the Soviet N1 Moon rocket on its pad on 19 September 1968. The NRO later said GAMBIT images confirmed the Soviets were building a vehicle to go to the Moon while they denied being in a Moon race.

space-project-horizon.title: Project Horizon
space-project-horizon.summary: Volume I of the US Army's 1959 study for a military outpost on the Moon, prepared by the Army Ballistic Missile Agency. It proposed a first manned landing in spring 1965 and an operational 12-man outpost by late 1966 at an estimated cost of six billion dollars.

space-mol-dorian.title: The DORIAN Files Revealed
space-mol-dorian.summary: The NRO's 2015 compendium on the Manned Orbiting Laboratory, built around Carl Berger's declassified history of the MOL program office and an index of the documents released with it. MOL was a 1960s Air Force space station whose secret DORIAN mission was for two-man crews to photograph Soviet military targets with a giant camera; it was cancelled in June 1969 without flying a crew.

ufo-flir1-tic-tac.title: FLIR1 (Tic Tac)
ufo-flir1-tic-tac.summary: Infrared targeting-pod video from a US Navy F/A-18 of the USS Nimitz strike group, recorded off Southern California on 14 November 2004 during the encounter pilots described as a white "Tic Tac". It leaked in 2007, the Pentagon released it officially in April 2020, and AARO lists it as unresolved.

ufo-gimbal.title: Gimbal
ufo-gimbal.summary: Infrared video from a US Navy F/A-18 of the USS Theodore Roosevelt strike group off the US East Coast in January 2015, in which the aircrew track an object that appears to rotate. It leaked in 2017, the Pentagon released it officially in April 2020, and AARO lists it as unresolved.

ufo-hottel-memo.title: Hottel Memo
ufo-hottel-memo.summary: A one-page memo of 22 March 1950 from Guy Hottel, head of the FBI's Washington field office, to J. Edgar Hoover, passing on a third party's story that an Air Force investigator said three "flying saucers" with three-foot-tall occupants had been recovered in New Mexico. It is the most viewed file in the FBI Vault; the FBI says it never investigated the claim and sees no reason to link it to Roswell.

ufo-apollo-17-dots.title: Apollo 17 Three Dots
ufo-apollo-17-dots.summary: A NASA photograph from the Apollo 17 mission in December 1972, published in the Pentagon's first PURSUE release with an enlarged inset of three faint dots in a triangle in the lunar sky. The Pentagon said there is no consensus on what they are; critics note the Apollo photos had been public for decades.
ufo-apollo-17-dots.credit: NASA (inset added by the Department of War)

ufo-roswell-case-closed.title: The Roswell Report: Case Closed
ufo-roswell-case-closed.summary: The US Air Force's 1997 report on the Roswell legend. It concludes that the "alien bodies" witnesses described were anthropomorphic test dummies carried aloft by high-altitude balloons, and that stories of bodies at the base hospital blended a 1956 KC-97 crash and a 1959 balloon accident.

ufo-gemini-7-bogey.title: Gemini 7 Bogey Audio
ufo-gemini-7-bogey.summary: NASA air-to-ground and public-affairs audio from the December 1965 Gemini VII flight, in which Frank Borman reports an unidentified object he calls a "bogey" to mission control in Houston. The Pentagon published it in its first PURSUE release in May 2026; space historian James Oberg attributes it to debris from the mission's own booster.

ufo-gofast.title: Go Fast
ufo-gofast.summary: Infrared video from a US Navy F/A-18F off the coast of Florida in January 2015 that seems to show a small object racing low over the ocean. The Pentagon released it officially in April 2020; AARO's February 2025 case resolution put the object at about 13,000 feet and found with high confidence that it did not move at anomalous speeds.

ufo-odni-preliminary-assessment.title: ODNI Preliminary Assessment on UAP
ufo-odni-preliminary-assessment.summary: The Director of National Intelligence's unclassified report to Congress on UAP, drafted with the Pentagon's UAP Task Force. Of 144 US government reports from 2004 to 2021 it could explain only one, a large deflating balloon, and it noted 18 incidents with unusual movement patterns or flight characteristics.
